samples.question: The sheet is off-white and carries one small framed inset. Exactly one mark in the whole figure is pure black: a single thin black trace inside that inset which runs continuously from its left end to its right end and has exactly one height at every horizontal position it covers. The guide height is the height of the trace's own left end, and the dotted grey line inside the inset is drawn at exactly that height. Follow the black trace from its left end rightwards. It first drops below the guide height. A return is a place where the trace comes back up and passes from below the guide height to above it; a dip that stays below the guide height is not a return, and passing from above back down to below is not a return either. Every turning point of the trace is at least sixteen pixels clear of the guide height, so the trace never merely touches that height and every return is a full crossing. Count every return along the whole trace, including the ones in its middle. The pale coloured curves, the other grey frames on the sheet and the short grey tick marks are decoration and carry no information. How many returns does the black trace make? Answer with one number: 1, 2, or 3.
